title: Why HDR-to-SDR Needs Tone Mapping, Not Just a New Label
description: HDR-to-SDR conversion needs tone mapping because an SDR output cannot represent the same highlight range as an HDR source.
direct: HDR-to-SDR conversion needs tone mapping because an SDR output cannot represent the same highlight range as an HDR source. A new codec, file extension or color label alone does not fit those highlights into the destination range.
figureAlt: A tall HDR brightness range maps smoothly into a shorter SDR range beside a sunlit photograph.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export. The diagram explains ranges, not actual HDR brightness or an App export.
cards.choice.heading: Map, then check
cards.choice.body: Tone mapping redistributes brightness into the output range. Clipping simply cuts values beyond a boundary, potentially making distinct bright details look the same. Neither method can recover texture already missing from the source.
sections.explain.heading: Why the result can look different
sections.explain.body: The conversion must decide how to represent highlights while keeping the main subject useful. Different tone-mapping pipelines can produce different contrast and highlight roll-off. A webpage illustration cannot demonstrate an HDR display’s real brightness or establish the quality of an App export.
sections.practice.heading: Use a defined delivery target
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops VideoFix. The current public release converts HDR into Rec.709 SDR and re-encodes the video; it does not promise lossless recovery or expose a claimed manual tone-curve editor here. The first three conversions are free, with a purchase required for more. Check the output in the destination workflow rather than judging only the original HDR preview.

steps.step-1.text: Keep the tagged HDR original. Identify the intended destination: use an SDR copy when the recipient requests standard Rec.709 SDR.
steps.step-2.text: In VideoFix: HDR Video Converter on iPhone, choose Convert HDR to SDR and export a separate H.264 MP4.
steps.step-3.text: Review faces, bright windows and shadow transitions in the saved copy and in the intended player. Retain the HDR original for future work.
